recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Heart Path of the Verdant One", "body": "Kyle Denton opens by tracing how the Green Man snared him, a solstice text about an up dog tea with yerba mate and holly landing at the exact moment his eyes crossed the words green man in an ebook. He recounts the Sufi story of Al Khidr, the Verdant One, meeting Moses, who had been trained for decades by the priests of Egypt and boasted that nobody could rival his intellect. Khidr tells him he could give the reason, but then they could no longer walk this path together. Denton frames it as Moses the mind and Khidr the heart, a trail that stops the moment he turns it cerebral."}, {"title": "Acanthus, Corinthian Pillars and the Crown of Thorns", "body": "The trail began in November, when a mutual friend, Topher, sent Denton a video about the acanthus leaf carved on Corinthian pillars, a plant he admits he knew nothing about even though his wife uses its swirling form throughout their zines and newsletters. The video argues the Greek word appears both in Genesis, where the ground is cursed with thorns, and in Matthew, where Jesus is crowned with them, though Denton notes the living plant does not appear to have thorns at all. Chance Garton adds that the cant inside the word is an old Gaelic term for speech, a hint that plants are themselves a secret language."}, {"title": "Holly King, Oak King and the Leaf Calendar", "body": "Denton walks through the plants that recur in Green Man carvings, hawthorn, oak, ivy, the fig and acanthus, noting they all share a deep lobed leaf that pushes visually outward from the center, which is why the carved face is described as disgorging foliage. He reads the motif as a calendar, with the holly king taking his mantle around Samhain and the oak king crowned at the summer solstice. He describes holly and hawthorn in tradition as plants of the heart, cites Dr Bach flower essence lore, and passes on his teacher Matthew Wood's account of a hawthorn tree saying it was learning how to become the oak."}, {"title": "Adam's Three Seeds and the Legend of the Rood", "body": "The group unpacks the medieval Legend of the Rood, drawn from a book of variant manuscripts. At Adam's death Seth petitions the angel of mercy and places three seeds in his father's mouth, from which cedar, pine and ash spring. Denton follows that wood through Moses's staff and the brazen serpent, then to Solomon, who cannot make the timber fit his temple and lays it across a stream until the Queen of Sheba refuses to walk on it, and finally to Golgotha as the cross. Garton ties the severed fecundity head to Berossus's account of Belus and to the root KRN behind kernel, horn and Kronos."}, {"title": "Wild Gods, Boundaries and Veriditas", "body": "In the final hour Garton catalogs the forest gods, the Etruscan Selvans, the Roman Sylvanus said by the obscure writer Dolabella to have set the first stones marking the limits of fields, Terminus at the property line, and Silenus with a laurel crown that reads as horns, arguing these are aspects of one god rather than separate deities. Denton closes with Elijah dropping his green mantle, with Milarepa turning green on a diet of nettles in the Tibetan mountains, and with St Hildegard von Bingen's veriditas, a greening power she set against what she called the drying power of sin, alongside Dickens's Ghost of Christmas Present."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The Mythographer of Fauna and Bio-Attuned Tincturist, Kyle Denton of Tippecanoe Herbs, returns to Vibe Rant to share his research on the mysterious primordial deity known as "The Green Man." Joining us are the highest ranking fellow initiates of the Great Whiteboard Brotherhood, PK and Slick Dissident.
